Subject: Question: micro-session billing behavior during pilot

Hi Evelyn,

Quick question from procurement as we sketch out the pilot SOW: our product makes a lot of very short inference calls — think 10–40 tokens — spread across many users and sessions. We want to understand two things before we finalize the SOW:

1) When calls are very short and frequent (many <50-token calls), how does Redwood aggregate/round those for billing? Is there per-call minimum or do you aggregate by conversation/session id?

2) How does long-context reuse (e.g., leveraging a KV cache for the same user across consecutive calls) affect billed tokens — is reused context deducted from the billable token count?

I attached a small sample of our traffic for one day (ACME_usage_samples.csv) — you can see lots of microcalls between 10:00–11:00.

Procurement is worried that rounding/minimums will make the pilot look much more expensive on paper than it will in steady state. Any clarity you can provide (preferably with a short example calc) would be helpful.

Thanks,
Maya Torres
Senior Procurement Manager, Acme Health

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question: micro-session billing behavior during pilot

Hi Maya — thanks for the sample and callout, this is exactly the kind of traffic pattern we anticipated for telehealth workflows. TL;DR: we bill at the token level with a configurable quantum and apply a short aggregation window for session stitching; cached KV tokens that are reused are not double-billed. Below is a concise breakdown + a worked example from your sample.

Key rules that will affect your invoice:
- Aggregation window: by default we group requests with the same conversation_id (or user-id) into a 60-minute stitching window for billing aggregation. That means multiple microcalls within an hour are combined for rounding/minimums.
- Rounding quantum: billing rounds up to the nearest 10-token quantum (configurable at contract time).
- Per-call minimum: for the hosted offering there is no per-API-call flat minimum if calls are aggregated; however if a request is completely isolated (no same-conversation requests within the stitching window) an implicit 50-token floor can apply — we can waive this for pilots.
- KV cache reuse: tokens present solely in the server-side KV cache (prefix/context reuse) are excluded from billable input tokens. Only newly sent prompt tokens + generated tokens are billable.

Worked example from your sample:
- You have three microcalls from the same user within 12 minutes: 12 tokens, 18 tokens, 9 tokens. Generated tokens each call: 22, 30, 15.
- Aggregate input tokens = 12+18+9 = 39; generated = 22+30+15 = 67.
- Apply rounding quantum (10-token): input rounds up to 40, generated rounds up to 70.
- Total billable tokens = 110 tokens for that stitched session; no per-call 50-token floor because it was stitched within window.

If those calls had been from different conversation_ids and isolated, each would round up and small calls could hit the implicit minimum (we can set that to 0 for pilots).

Proposed concessions for the pilot (to address procurement concerns):
- Waive the implicit per-call 50-token minimum for the first 90 days.
- Apply quantum = 10 tokens.
- Provide a one-time smoothing credit equal to the difference between per-call minimums and stitched billing for the first 30 days if usage is below 250k tokens.

I'll loop in Karthik for a quick note on the KV technical side and Markus on commercial if you want to turn this into contractual language. Happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk procurement through one or two sample invoices — when are you available?

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Enterprise Accounts — Redwood Inference

Hi Maya — Camila from Product Pricing here, looping Karthik for the KV cache/serving nuance and Markus for commercial confirmation. Quick answers:

1) Stitching window: it is sliding. For each incoming request we look back over the configured window (default 60 minutes) for the same conversation_id/user-id. That handles bursts that begin mid-hour without splitting them into separate buckets.

2) Smoothing credit: we typically post it as a separate invoice line ("Pilot smoothing credit") so procurement sees the deduction clearly. We can also provide a separate reconciliation report for the first billing period.

3) Dedicated vs Hosted: the core billing primitives are the same (token quantum and cache exclusion). Where Dedicated differs is commercial: reserved capacity customers get committed-token pricing and can negotiate smaller quanta or explicit per-request floors as part of the contract. For your move-to-dedicated scenario we can:
   - Set quantum to 5 tokens (if committed volume warrants), or
   - Offer a blended seat+token SKU where burst microcalls are amortized against a seat allowance, reducing invoice volatility.

Karthik — short technical note we can forward to Acme: KV cache tokens are not counted as billable when they are purely server-side reused data. However, if the client sends the entire long context with every request (rather than relying on server-managed KV identifiers/prefix references) then those client-sent tokens are billable. For streaming calls that append long history only once and then send deltas, the billed tokens follow the delta + generation tokens model.

Next steps I propose for the pilot SOW:
- We document the sliding 60-minute stitching behavior in the SOW appendix.
- Redwood to waive the 50-token per-call floor for 90 days.
- Redwood to include a pilot smoothing credit line on invoices for month 1.
- Schedule Wed 21 May 10:15 PT for a 30-min recon call to walk the sample invoice (Evelyn, adding a calendar invite).

Cheers,
Camila Reyes
Principal, Product Pricing — Redwood Inference
